directionAnswers.topic: Helping adult children support their parents’ daily health habits

stageHistory.stage: Inspecting website imagery and choosing useful angles

writerRun.review: category-evidence-v10: All four posts are grounded in the supplied website evidence. Dedicated-doctor oversight, coordinated care, weekly doctor involvement, monthly family reports and consideration of food preferences are supported; no health outcomes, testimonials or participant identities are invented. The homepage supports the free-consultation offer and destination. Both three-slide carousels progress from a recognisable adult-child concern to coordinated support and a concrete distinction between clinical involvement and family updates. The statics provide a complementary buying idea: personalisation includes what a parent will actually eat, with practical consultation preparation in the captions. The supplied older-woman portrait provides relevant human context without being presented as proof of programme participation. All six approved decisions are respected: enquiry next steps, personalised programmes, health-and-wellness service framing, support for parents’ daily habits, warm wording and advice-led promotion. This assessment covers the structured copy and asset choices, not rendered visuals.
